title: Natural Domain and Range of a Radical Transformation
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Natural Domain and Range
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain and range of the real-valued function f(x) = 1 - \sqrt{x}.

steps.title: Formulate Radicand Non-Negativity Condition
steps.explanation: The formula involves the principal square root sqrt(x). In the real number system, the square root of a negative number is undefined.
steps.why: Even-indexed roots are defined in R only when the radicand is non-negative.

steps.title: State the Domain
steps.explanation: There are no other operations restricting the input, so the natural domain is all non-negative real numbers, [0, inf).
steps.why: The radical is the sole algebraic restriction governing the formula.

steps.title: Analyze the Range
steps.explanation: The square root sqrt(x) outputs all values in [0, inf). Multiplying by -1 reverses the inequality, yielding values in (-inf, 0]. Adding 1 shifts the values up by 1, resulting in all values less than or equal to 1.
steps.why: Multiplying an inequality by a negative number reverses the direction of the inequality.

steps.title: State the Range in Interval Notation
steps.explanation: At x = 0, f(0) = 1 - 0 = 1. As x increases without bound, sqrt(x) grows without bound, so 1 - sqrt(x) approaches negative infinity, covering all values in (-inf, 1].
steps.why: The square root function is strictly increasing and unbounded above on its domain.
